name: Stored Data Manipulation
description:
Adversaries may insert, delete, or manipulate data at rest in order to influence external outcomes or hide activity, thus threatening the integrity of the data.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)(Citation: DOJ Lazarus Sony 2018) By manipulating stored data, adversaries may attempt to affect a business process, organizational understanding, and decision making.

Stored data could include a variety of file formats, such as Office files, databases, stored emails, and custom file formats. The type of modification and the impact it will have depends on the type of data as well as the goals and objectives of the adversary. For complex systems, an adversary would likely need special expertise and possibly access to specialized software related to the system that would typically be gained through a prolonged information gathering campaign in order to have the desired impact.

references.description: Department of Justice. (2018, September 6). Criminal Complaint - United States of America v. PARK JIN HYOK. Retrieved March 29, 2019.
FireEye. (2018, October 03). APT38: Un-usual Suspects. Retrieved November 17, 2024.

telemetry.name: File Creation
telemetry.description: Creation or overwrite of a file at an observed path.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope Sysmon FileCreate (11) to the lab directory; retain the process and file path. Differentiate creation/overwrite if the sensor can.

providers.name: Microsoft Sysmon
providers.scope: Windows event-based collection; enable the event types needed below.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: Linux alternative for supported system-call and file events; different semantics and fields.

providers.name: Apple Endpoint Security clients
providers.scope: macOS alternative where the subscribed event exists; requires an entitled, approved client, not an iOS collector.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Event filtering and sensor versions change coverage. High-volume image-load and process-access collection needs tuning; endpoint events alone do not establish intent.

telemetry.anomaly_design: Per host role and user: rare process/object combinations, bursts of object access or modification, and ordered parent/action sequences. Compare maintenance windows and signed software rollout activity.

telemetry.name: File Deletion
telemetry.description: Deletion of a file, with path and responsible process where available.
telemetry.collection_focus: Prefer Sysmon FileDeleteDetected (26) when content retention is not needed; FileDelete (23) also archives files and requires a storage/privacy plan.

telemetry.name: File Metadata
telemetry.description: File attributes such as path, size, timestamps, ownership and cryptographic hash.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect scoped file inventory/FIM metadata with hash algorithm and observation time; preserve original timestamps separately from collector time.

providers.name: osquery
providers.scope: Scheduled host-state queries; supported tables and privileges vary by OS. Select a table that actually exposes the required object.

providers.name: Linux Audit plus inventory snapshots
providers.scope: Events explain changes; snapshots describe state at collection time.

configuration: Define the inventory query, allowed host set, interval and least-privileged reader. Store a stable asset ID, observation time and collector version.
Keep successive snapshots and calculate additions, removals and changed attributes. Pair state changes with audit events when available.
Export collector health and missed-poll counts so a missing snapshot is not misclassified as a missing asset.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Snapshots miss short-lived objects and do not identify who caused a change. A generic inventory agent is not guaranteed to expose firmware or kernel-level details.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Compare authorized state snapshots: first-seen drivers/services/modules, unexpected configuration drift and integrity changes. Record collection cadence; absence in a sample is not evidence of deletion.

telemetry.name: File Modification
telemetry.description: Changes to file data or attributes.
telemetry.collection_focus: Use file-integrity monitoring or scoped OS file-write auditing for general changes. Sysmon 2 records creation-time changes; it is not a general file-write event.

strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Stored Data Manipulation across OS Platforms.

analytics.name: Analytic 0555
analytics.guidance: Identify unauthorized creation, deletion, or modification of business-critical stored data such as Office documents, database files, and log archives. Detect anomalous processes modifying stored data outside of expected workflows (e.g., non-database processes modifying database files).

tuning.description: Paths to sensitive stored data files such as database directories or email archives.
List of legitimate processes expected to create, delete, or modify stored data.
Threshold for correlating multiple suspicious file operations within a short period.

analytics.name: Analytic 0556
analytics.guidance: Detect suspicious file creation, modification, or deletion in stored data directories (e.g., `/var/lib/mysql/`, `/var/log/`, mail spools). Identify shell commands interacting directly with structured data files instead of legitimate database utilities.

tuning.description: Environment-specific paths where business-critical stored data resides.
Legitimate scripts/utilities excluded to minimize false positives.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: open, unlink, rename: File creation or deletion involving critical stored data

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: write: Modification of structured stored data by suspicious processes

analytics.name: Analytic 0557
analytics.guidance: Monitor sensitive data files such as plist-based storage, mail archives, or Office files for unexpected modifications. Detect anomalous processes modifying stored data outside expected update cycles using FSEvents and Unified Logs.

tuning.description: Baseline hash values or metadata for stored data files to detect manipulation.
Whitelisted applications permitted to update stored data (e.g., Outlook, MySQL).

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Unexpected creation or modification of stored data files in protected directories

log_sources.name: macos:osquery
log_sources.channel: CREATE, DELETE, WRITE: Stored data manipulation attempts by unauthorized processes

software.name: SUNSPOT
software.description: [SUNSPOT](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0562) created a copy of the SolarWinds Orion software source file with a .bk extension to backup the original content, wrote [SUNBURST](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0559) using the same filename but with a .tmp extension, and then moved [SUNBURST](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0559) using MoveFileEx to the original filename with a .cs extension so it could be compiled within Orion software.(Citation: CrowdStrike SUNSPOT Implant January 2021)

references.description: CrowdStrike Intelligence Team. (2021, January 11). SUNSPOT: An Implant in the Build Process. Retrieved January 11, 2021.

software.name: MultiLayer Wiper
software.description: [MultiLayer Wiper](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1135) changes the original path information of deleted files to make recovery efforts more difficult.(Citation: Unit42 Agrius 2023)

references.description: Or Chechik, Tom Fakterman, Daniel Frank & Assaf Dahan. (2023, November 6). Agonizing Serpens (Aka Agrius) Targeting the Israeli Higher Education and Tech Sectors. Retrieved May 22, 2024.

actors.name: APT38
actors.description: [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used DYEPACK to create, delete, and alter records in databases used for SWIFT transactions.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)

references.description: FireEye. (2018, October 03). APT38: Un-usual Suspects. Retrieved November 17, 2024.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.description: Ensure least privilege principles are applied to important information resources to reduce exposure to data manipulation risk.

mitigations.name: Remote Data Storage
mitigations.description: Consider implementing IT disaster recovery plans that contain procedures for taking regular data backups that can be used to restore organizational data.(Citation: Ready.gov IT DRP) Ensure backups are stored off system and is protected from common methods adversaries may use to gain access and manipulate backups.

references.description: Ready.gov. (n.d.). IT Disaster Recovery Plan. Retrieved March 15, 2019.

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.description: Consider encrypting important information to reduce an adversary’s ability to perform tailored data modifications.

simulation.prerequisites: Use disposable lab hosts and test accounts, explicit target allowlists, a clean snapshot, bounded egress and a restore plan. Review every candidate and dependency before any execution.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
